source.text: כְּדַבֵּ֤ר אֶפְרַ֨יִם֙ רְתֵ֔ת נָשָׂ֥א ה֖וּא בְּיִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַיֶּאְשַׁ֥ם בַּבַּ֖עַל וַיָּמֹֽת׃

records.literal_gloss: When spoke Ephraim, trembling; lifted up he [was] in Israel; and he became guilty through the Baal, and he died.

en.L: When Ephraim spoke, [there was] trembling; \q he was lifted up in Israel; \q but he became guilty through Baal, and he died.
en.B: When Ephraim spoke, people trembled; \q he was exalted in Israel. \q But he became guilty through Baal, and he died.
en.R: Once, when Ephraim spoke, people trembled. \q Ephraim was honored in Israel. \q But Ephraim sinned by worshiping Baal, and that sin brought death.

es.L: Cuando Efraín hablaba, [había] temblor; \q era exaltado en Israel; \q pero se hizo culpable por Baal, y murió.
es.B: Cuando Efraín hablaba, la gente temblaba; \q era ensalzado en Israel. \q Pero se hizo culpable por Baal, y murió.
es.R: En otro tiempo, cuando Efraín hablaba, la gente temblaba. \q Efraín era honrado en Israel. \q Pero Efraín pecó adorando a Baal, y ese pecado le trajo la muerte.

ko.L: 에브라임이 말하면 [모두가] 떨었다. \q 그는 이스라엘에서 높임을 받았다. \q 그러나 그가 바알 때문에 죄를 지어 죽었다.
ko.B: 에브라임이 말하면 사람들이 떨었다. \q 그는 이스라엘에서 높임을 받았다. \q 그러나 그는 바알 때문에 죄를 지었고, 그래서 죽었다.
ko.R: 전에는 에브라임이 말하면 사람들이 떨었다. \q 에브라임은 이스라엘에서 존경을 받았다. \q 그러나 에브라임은 바알을 섬겨 죄를 지었고, 그 죄가 죽음을 불러왔다.

fr.L: Quand Éphraïm parlait, [c’était] l’effroi ; \q il était élevé en Israël ; \q mais il s’est rendu coupable par Baal, et il est mort.
fr.B: Quand Éphraïm parlait, on tremblait ; \q il était élevé en Israël. \q Mais il s’est rendu coupable par Baal, et il est mort.
fr.R: Autrefois, quand Éphraïm parlait, les gens tremblaient. \q Éphraïm était honoré en Israël. \q Mais Éphraïm a péché en adorant Baal, et ce péché lui a apporté la mort.

sw.L: Efraimu aliponena, [palikuwa na] kutetemeka; \q alikuwa ametukuzwa katika Israeli; \q lakini alipata hatia kwa Baali, akafa.
sw.B: Efraimu aliposema, watu walitetemeka; \q alikuwa ametukuka katika Israeli. \q Lakini alipata hatia kwa sababu ya Baali, akafa.
sw.R: Zamani, Efraimu aliposema, watu walitetemeka. \q Efraimu aliheshimiwa katika Israeli. \q Lakini Efraimu alitenda dhambi kwa kumwabudu Baali, na dhambi hiyo ikamletea kifo.

vi.L: Khi Ép-ra-im nói, [người ta] run sợ; \q nó được tôn cao trong Y-sơ-ra-ên; \q nhưng nó đã mắc tội vì Ba-anh, và nó đã chết.
vi.B: Khi Ép-ra-im lên tiếng, người ta run sợ; \q nó được tôn trọng trong Y-sơ-ra-ên. \q Nhưng nó đã mắc tội vì Ba-anh, và nó đã chết.
vi.R: Xưa kia, khi Ép-ra-im lên tiếng, người ta run sợ. \q Ép-ra-im được tôn trọng trong Y-sơ-ra-ên. \q Nhưng Ép-ra-im đã phạm tội thờ Ba-anh, và tội ấy đã đem đến sự chết.

decisions.choice: when Ephraim spoke, others trembled: his word carried weight among the tribes
alternatives: Ephraim spoke with trembling, humbly, and so was lifted up
decisions.reason: The word for trembling is found only here and in Jeremiah 49:24, where it means panic. The clause has no subject for the trembling, so it may be the fear that Ephraim's word caused in others, or Ephraim's own humble fear. Ephraim was the leading tribe of the north: Joshua and Jeroboam I came from it (Joshua 19:50; 1 Kings 11:26), and it expected to be consulted (Judges 8:1-3; 12:1). The verse sets that past honor against the fall that follows.

decisions.choice: guilty through Baal: the worship of Baal, the Canaanite storm god, as in 2:10, 15 and 11:2
decisions.reason: Hosea repeatedly charges Israel with giving Baal the credit and the offerings that belong to the LORD (2:10, 15, 18-19; 11:2). Here that worship is named as the point where Ephraim's guilt began.

decisions.choice: he died: Ephraim's ruin as a people, spoken of as already done
alternatives: the death of individual worshipers
decisions.reason: The verb is a past form, but the nation still exists in the verses that follow. Its doom is so certain that it can be called death already, as Amos 5:2 laments fallen Israel. The theme of death runs through the chapter to 13:14.

decisions.choice: sinned by worshiping Baal, and that sin brought death
alternatives: became guilty through Baal, and he died
decisions.reason: Readable says what "through Baal" means and makes plain that the death is the result of the guilt (m2, m3). It names Ephraim three times instead of using "he", so the reader does not lose track of who is meant.

source.text: וְעַתָּ֣ה׀יוֹסִ֣פוּ לַחֲטֹ֗א וַיַּעְשׂ֣וּ לָהֶם֩ מַסֵּכָ֨ה מִכַּסְפָּ֤ם כִּתְבוּנָם֙ עֲצַבִּ֔ים מַעֲשֵׂ֥ה חָרָשִׁ֖ים כֻּלֹּ֑ה לָהֶם֙ הֵ֣ם אֹמְרִ֔ים זֹבְחֵ֣י אָדָ֔ם עֲגָלִ֖ים יִשָּׁקֽוּן׃

records.literal_gloss: And now they add to sin, and they have made for themselves a cast image from their silver, according to their skill idols; work of craftsmen all of it; of them they [are] saying, sacrificers of humankind calves they kiss.

en.L: And now they add to [their] sinning, and they have made for themselves a cast image from their silver, idols by their own skill; \q the work of craftsmen [is] all of it. \q Of them they say, \q "Sacrificers of humankind kiss calves!"
en.B: Now they sin more and more and have made themselves a cast image from their silver, idols shaped by their own skill, \q every one of them the work of craftsmen. \q People say of them, \q "Human beings who offer sacrifice kiss calves!"
en.R: Now they sin more and more. They melt down their silver and skillfully make idols, \q all of them made by craftsmen. \q People say about them, \q "These humans offer sacrifices and kiss statues of calves!"

es.L: Y ahora añaden a [su] pecar, y se han hecho una imagen fundida de su plata, ídolos según su habilidad; \q obra de artesanos [es] todo ello. \q De ellos dicen: \q «¡Los que sacrifican hombres besan becerros!».
es.B: Ahora pecan más y más, y se han hecho de su plata una imagen fundida, ídolos formados con su propia habilidad, \q todos ellos obra de artesanos. \q La gente dice de ellos: \q «¡Seres humanos que ofrecen sacrificios besan becerros!».
es.R: Ahora pecan más y más. Funden su plata y con habilidad hacen ídolos, \q todos hechos por artesanos. \q La gente dice de ellos: \q «¡Estos seres humanos ofrecen sacrificios y besan estatuas de becerros!».

ko.L: 이제 그들이 [죄에] 죄를 더하여, 자기 은으로 자기들을 위해 부어 만든 형상을, 자기 솜씨대로 우상들을 만들었다. \q 그것은 모두 장인들이 만든 것이다. \q 그들을 두고 사람들이 말한다. \q "사람 가운데 제사 드리는 자들이 송아지들에게 입을 맞춘다!"
ko.B: 이제 그들은 죄에 죄를 더하여, 은을 녹여 부어 만든 형상을 만들고, 자기 솜씨대로 우상들을 빚었다. \q 그것들은 모두 장인들의 작품이다. \q 사람들이 그들을 두고 말한다. \q "제사를 드리는 사람들이 송아지들에게 입을 맞춘다!"
ko.R: 이제 그들은 점점 더 많은 죄를 짓는다. 은을 녹여 솜씨 좋게 우상들을 만든다. \q 그것들은 모두 기술자들이 만든 것이다. \q 사람들이 그들을 두고 말한다. \q "이 사람들이 제물을 바치고 송아지 상에게 입을 맞춘다!"

fr.L: Et maintenant ils ajoutent à [leur] péché, et ils se sont fait de leur argent une image de métal fondu, des idoles selon leur habileté ; \q œuvre d’artisans, tout cela. \q D’eux ils disent : \q « Ceux qui sacrifient [des] humains embrassent des veaux ! »
fr.B: Maintenant ils pèchent de plus en plus ; ils se sont fait avec leur argent une image de métal fondu, des idoles façonnées avec habileté, \q toutes œuvre d’artisans. \q On dit d’eux : \q « Des humains qui offrent des sacrifices embrassent des veaux ! »
fr.R: Maintenant ils pèchent de plus en plus. Ils font fondre leur argent et fabriquent des idoles avec habileté, \q toutes faites par des artisans. \q Les gens disent à leur sujet : \q « Ces humains offrent des sacrifices et embrassent des statues de veaux ! »

sw.L: Na sasa wanaongeza kutenda dhambi, nao wamejifanyia sanamu ya kusubu kwa fedha yao, sanamu kwa ustadi wao wenyewe; \q yote [ni] kazi ya mafundi. \q Juu yao wanasema, \q "Watoa dhabihu wa wanadamu wanabusu ndama!"
sw.B: Sasa wanazidi kutenda dhambi, nao wamejitengenezea sanamu ya kusubu kwa fedha yao, sanamu zilizoundwa kwa ustadi wao wenyewe, \q zote zikiwa kazi ya mafundi. \q Watu husema juu yao, \q "Wanadamu wanaotoa dhabihu wanabusu ndama!"
sw.R: Sasa wanazidi kutenda dhambi. Wanayeyusha fedha yao na kutengeneza sanamu kwa ustadi, \q zote zikiwa zimetengenezwa na mafundi. \q Watu husema juu yao, \q "Watu hawa wanatoa dhabihu na kubusu sanamu za ndama!"

vi.L: Bây giờ chúng phạm tội thêm nữa, và đã đúc cho mình tượng đúc bằng bạc, những thần tượng theo sự khéo léo của chúng; \q tất cả đều [là] công việc của thợ thủ công. \q Người ta nói về chúng: \q "Những kẻ dâng sinh tế là loài người lại hôn bò con!"
vi.B: Bây giờ chúng càng phạm tội thêm, lấy bạc mình đúc tượng, làm những thần tượng theo tài khéo của mình, \q tất cả đều là công việc của thợ thủ công. \q Người ta nói về chúng: \q "Loài người dâng sinh tế mà lại hôn bò con!"
vi.R: Bây giờ chúng phạm tội ngày càng nhiều. Chúng nấu chảy bạc của mình và khéo léo làm ra các thần tượng, \q tất cả đều do thợ thủ công làm ra. \q Người ta nói về chúng: \q "Những con người này dâng sinh tế và hôn tượng bò con!"

decisions.choice: kiss calves: kissing the calf images as an act of worship
decisions.reason: The calves are the bull images set up by Jeroboam I at Bethel and Dan (1 Kings 12:28-29), which Hosea mocks as "the calf of Samaria" (8:5-6; 10:5). Kissing an image, or kissing the hand toward it, was a sign of worship (1 Kings 19:18; Job 31:26-27).

decisions.choice: sacrificers of humankind: human beings who offer sacrifice, bowing to calves
alternatives: those who sacrifice human beings, that is, human sacrifice
a command: "Let those who sacrifice kiss the calves"
"to them they say": words spoken to the worshipers rather than about them
decisions.reason: The two Hebrew words can mean "those among humankind who sacrifice" or "those who sacrifice human beings". The first fits the mockery of the verse: people kiss animals, and idols that are only the work of craftsmen. Hosea does not elsewhere charge Israel with human sacrifice, though 2 Kings 17:17 says the northern kingdom practiced it. The words before the saying can mean "to them" or "of them", and the verb "kiss" can be read as a command. The Hebrew is compressed, and every reading is possible.

decisions.choice: the work of craftsmen: idols are things people make
decisions.reason: The same charge is made in 8:4-6 ("a craftsman made it; it is not God") and returns in 14:4 ("the work of our hands"). The cast image is metal poured into a mold (Exodus 32:4, 8).

decisions.choice: melt down their silver; statues of calves
alternatives: make a cast image from their silver; calves
decisions.reason: Readable explains that a cast image is made by melting metal and that the calves are images, not live animals (m1, m3). It keeps "humans" so the reader can see the irony of people kissing calves (m2).

decisions.choice: "Los que sacrifican hombres"
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew phrase, which can be read as people who offer sacrifice or as people who sacrifice humans; the meaning decision gives the first reading, which Balanced and Readable follow.

source.text: לָכֵ֗ן יִֽהְיוּ֙ כַּעֲנַן־בֹּ֔קֶר וְכַטַּ֖ל מַשְׁכִּ֣ים הֹלֵ֑ךְ כְּמֹץ֙ יְסֹעֵ֣ר מִגֹּ֔רֶן וּכְעָשָׁ֖ן מֵאֲרֻבָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore they will be like a cloud of [the] morning, and like the dew early going away, like chaff [that] is storm-driven from a threshing floor, and like smoke from a window.

en.L: Therefore they will be like the morning cloud, \q and like the dew that goes away early, \q like chaff that is whirled away from a threshing floor, \q and like smoke from a window.
en.B: So they will be like the morning mist, \q like the dew that vanishes early, \q like chaff swept by a storm from the threshing floor, \q like smoke drifting out through a window.
en.R: So they will disappear like morning mist, \q like dew that is soon gone, \q like straw blown off a threshing floor by the wind, \q like smoke that drifts out a window.

es.L: Por tanto serán como la nube de la mañana, \q y como el rocío que temprano se va, \q como el tamo que el torbellino arrebata de la era, \q y como el humo que sale por la ventana.
es.B: Por eso serán como la niebla de la mañana, \q como el rocío que desaparece temprano, \q como la paja que la tormenta barre de la era, \q como el humo que se escapa por una ventana.
es.R: Por eso desaparecerán como la niebla de la mañana, \q como el rocío que pronto se va, \q como la paja que el viento se lleva de la era, \q como el humo que sale por una ventana.

ko.L: 그러므로 그들은 아침 구름 같고, \q 일찍 사라지는 이슬 같고, \q 타작마당에서 회오리바람에 날리는 겨 같고, \q 창문에서 나가는 연기 같을 것이다.
ko.B: 그러므로 그들은 아침 안개 같고, \q 이른 아침에 사라지는 이슬 같고, \q 타작마당에서 폭풍에 날려 가는 겨 같고, \q 창문 밖으로 빠져나가는 연기 같을 것이다.
ko.R: 그래서 그들은 아침 안개처럼 사라질 것이다. \q 금방 없어지는 이슬처럼, \q 바람에 타작마당에서 날려 가는 겨처럼, \q 창문 밖으로 흩어지는 연기처럼 사라질 것이다.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi ils seront comme le nuage du matin, \q et comme la rosée qui s’en va de bonne heure, \q comme la balle emportée par le tourbillon loin de l’aire, \q et comme la fumée [qui sort] d’une fenêtre.
fr.B: Alors ils seront comme la brume du matin, \q comme la rosée qui disparaît tôt, \q comme la balle que la tempête chasse de l’aire, \q comme la fumée qui s’échappe par une fenêtre.
fr.R: Alors ils disparaîtront comme la brume du matin, \q comme la rosée qui s’en va vite, \q comme la paille que le vent emporte loin de l’aire de battage, \q comme la fumée qui sort par une fenêtre.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo watakuwa kama wingu la asubuhi, \q na kama umande unaotoweka mapema, \q kama makapi yanayopeperushwa na kimbunga kutoka uwanja wa kupuria, \q na kama moshi kutoka dirishani.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo watakuwa kama ukungu wa asubuhi, \q kama umande unaotoweka mapema mchana, \q kama makapi yanayopeperushwa na dhoruba kutoka uwanja wa kupuria, \q kama moshi unaotoka dirishani.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo watatoweka kama ukungu wa asubuhi, \q kama umande unaokauka mara jua linapochomoza, \q kama makapi yanayopeperushwa na upepo kutoka uwanja wa kupuria, \q kama moshi unaotoka dirishani.

vi.L: Vì vậy chúng sẽ như mây buổi sáng, \q như sương móc sớm tan đi, \q như trấu bị gió lốc cuốn khỏi sân đạp lúa, \q như khói bay ra từ cửa sổ.
vi.B: Vì thế chúng sẽ như sương mù buổi sáng, \q như giọt sương tan biến lúc sớm mai, \q như trấu bị bão cuốn khỏi sân đạp lúa, \q như khói bay qua cửa sổ.
vi.R: Vì thế chúng sẽ biến mất như sương mù buổi sáng, \q như giọt sương tan đi ngay sau khi mặt trời mọc, \q như rơm rác bị gió thổi bay khỏi sân đạp lúa, \q như khói bay ra ngoài cửa sổ.

decisions.choice: the morning cloud and the early dew: the same pictures as 6:4, now used for the people themselves
decisions.reason: In 6:4 God says that Israel's loyal love is "like a morning cloud, like the dew that goes away early". Love that does not last leads to a people that does not last. In 14:6 the picture is turned around: God himself will be like dew to Israel.

decisions.choice: chaff from a threshing floor; smoke from a window: things that are blown away and gone
decisions.reason: Grain was threshed on an open, raised floor, and the wind carried the light chaff away (Psalm 1:4; Isaiah 17:13). Houses had no chimneys: smoke went out through an opening in the wall or roof, often covered with a lattice. The word is used for the "windows" of heaven in Genesis 7:11.

decisions.choice: they will disappear like ...
alternatives: they will be like ...
decisions.reason: Readable states the point that all four pictures share, so that a young reader does not have to work it out.

decisions.choice: the first two lines as 6:4
decisions.reason: The same pictures as 6:4, so each level keeps its wording from there.

decisions.choice: The first two lines reuse 6:4 at each level
decisions.reason: Hosea uses the same pictures again, now for the people themselves; Korean keeps the 6:4 wording so the echo is heard.

decisions.choice: the first two lines in the words of 6:4 ("nuage du matin", "la rosée qui s'en va de bonne heure" at L; "la brume du matin", "la rosée qui disparaît" at B)
alternatives: new wording
decisions.reason: The meaning decision points back to 6:4, so the French repeats its pictures in the same words.

decisions.choice: the first two lines as 6:4
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats the pictures of 6:4 (m1), so each level reuses its wording there.

decisions.choice: the morning cloud and the early dew in the words of 6:4 at each level
decisions.reason: The same pictures as 6:4, so each level keeps that verse's wording.

source.text: וְאָנֹכִ֛י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהֶ֖יךָ מֵאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרָ֑יִם וֵאלֹהִ֤ים זֽוּלָתִי֙ לֹ֣א תֵדָ֔ע וּמוֹשִׁ֥יעַ אַ֖יִן בִּלְתִּֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: And I [am] Yahweh your God from [the] land of Egypt, and a god besides me you do not know, and a savior there is not except me.

en.L: But I [am] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God from the land of Egypt; \q you know no god besides {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \q and there is no savior except {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: But I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God, and have been since the land of Egypt; \q you are to know no god but {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, \q and there is no savior except {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: I am {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God. I have been your God since you were in Egypt. \q You must not know any god but {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. \q No one else can save you.

es.L: Pero yo [soy] {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios desde la tierra de Egipto; \q no conoces otro dios fuera de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, \q y no hay salvador sino yo.
es.B: Pero yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios, y lo he sido desde la tierra de Egipto; \q no has de conocer otro dios fuera de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, \q y no hay salvador sino yo.
es.R: Yo soy {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} tu Dios. He sido tu Dios desde que estabas en Egipto. \q No debes conocer a ningún otro dios fuera de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}. \q Nadie más puede salvarte.

ko.L: 그러나 나는 이집트 땅에서부터 너의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}다. \q 너는 나 외에 다른 신을 알지 못하고, \q 나 말고는 구원자가 없다.
ko.B: 그러나 나는 네가 이집트 땅에 있을 때부터 너의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}다. \q 너는 나 말고 다른 신을 알아서는 안 된다. \q 나 말고는 구원자가 없다.
ko.R: 나는 너의 하나님 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}다. 네가 이집트에 있을 때부터 나는 너의 하나님이었다. \q 너는 나 말고 다른 신을 알아서는 안 된다. \q 너를 구원할 이는 나밖에 없다.

fr.L: Mais {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, [je suis] {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu depuis le pays d’Égypte ; \q tu ne connais pas d’autre dieu que {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, \q et il n’y a pas de sauveur en dehors de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.
fr.B: Mais je suis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu, et je le suis depuis le pays d’Égypte ; \q tu ne dois connaître aucun autre dieu que {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, \q et il n’y a pas d’autre sauveur que {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}.
fr.R: Je suis {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} ton Dieu. Je suis ton Dieu depuis le temps où tu étais en Égypte. \q Tu ne dois connaître aucun autre dieu que {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. \q Personne d’autre ne peut te sauver.

sw.L: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} [ni] {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako tangu nchi ya Misri; \q hujui mungu mwingine ila {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, \q wala hakuna mwokozi isipokuwa {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}.
sw.B: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} ni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako, tangu nchi ya Misri; \q usimjue mungu mwingine ila {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, \q wala hakuna mwokozi isipokuwa {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}.
sw.R: Mimi ni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} Mungu wako. Nimekuwa Mungu wako tangu ulipokuwa Misri. \q Usimjue mungu mwingine ila {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}. \q Hakuna mwingine awezaye kukuokoa.

vi.L: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} [là] {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời ngươi từ đất Ai Cập; \q ngươi không biết thần nào ngoài {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, \q và ngoài {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không có đấng cứu rỗi nào.
vi.B: Nhưng {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời ngươi từ khi ngươi còn ở đất Ai Cập; \q ngươi không được biết thần nào ngoài {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, \q và ngoài {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} không có đấng cứu rỗi nào.
vi.R: Ta là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Đức Chúa Trời ngươi. Ta đã là Đức Chúa Trời ngươi từ khi ngươi còn ở Ai Cập. \q Ngươi không được biết thần nào khác ngoài {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. \q Không ai khác có thể cứu ngươi.

decisions.choice: the words that begin the Ten Commandments
decisions.reason: "I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt ... you shall have no other gods besides me" (Exodus 20:2-3; Deuteronomy 5:6-7). Hosea used "your God from the land of Egypt" already in 12:10. "From the land of Egypt" means from the time God brought them out.

decisions.choice: you know no god but me: both a fact of the covenant and a command
alternatives: only a statement: you have known no other god
only a command: you shall not know any other god
decisions.reason: The verb form can describe what is or say what must be, and the echo of the commandment suggests both. To "know" God in Hosea means to acknowledge him and live loyally with him (2:22; 4:1; 6:3, 6).

decisions.choice: the Hebrew text, which goes straight on from "I am the LORD your God" to "from the land of Egypt"
alternatives: the longer Greek text, which adds lines about God making the heavens and the earth
decisions.reason: The Septuagint has a longer verse here, with a description of God as the maker of heaven and earth and of the heavenly host. The Hebrew text has no such lines, and the translation follows it.

decisions.choice: ever since the land of Egypt (B); since you were in Egypt (R)
alternatives: from the land of Egypt
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make plain that "from" means "since the time of" (m1). Readable turns "no savior except me" into "no one else can save you", which says the same thing in plainer words.

decisions.choice: "sino yo"
decisions.reason: Spanish says "except me" with the subject form "yo", which takes no deity_pronoun span, as God's own "yo" never does.

decisions.choice: the first line as 12:10
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats 12:10, so the Swahili repeats its wording at each level.

records.literal_gloss: I knew you in the wilderness, in a land of droughts.

en.L: I knew you in the wilderness, \q in a land of drought.
en.B: I cared for you in the wilderness, \q in a land of burning drought.
en.R: I took care of you in the desert, \q in a dry land with no water.

es.L: Yo te conocí en el desierto, \q en tierra de sequía.
es.B: Yo cuidé de ti en el desierto, \q en una tierra de sequía ardiente.
es.R: Yo te cuidé en el desierto, \q en una tierra seca y sin agua.

ko.L: 내가 광야에서, \q 메마른 땅에서 너를 알았다.
ko.B: 내가 광야에서, \q 타는 듯한 메마른 땅에서 너를 돌보았다.
ko.R: 나는 사막에서, \q 물 한 방울 없는 메마른 땅에서 너를 돌보았다.

fr.L: Moi, je t’ai connu dans le désert, \q dans une terre de sécheresse.
fr.B: J’ai pris soin de toi dans le désert, \q dans une terre brûlée par la sécheresse.
fr.R: Je {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} suis occupé de toi dans le désert, \q dans un pays sec, sans eau.

sw.L: Mimi nilikujua nyikani, \q katika nchi ya ukame.
sw.B: Nilikutunza jangwani, \q katika nchi ya ukame mkali.
sw.R: Nilikutunza jangwani, \q katika nchi kavu isiyo na maji.

vi.L: Ta đã biết ngươi trong hoang mạc, \q trong đất khô hạn.
vi.B: Ta đã chăm sóc ngươi trong hoang mạc, \q trong xứ khô cháy.
vi.R: Ta đã chăm lo cho ngươi trong sa mạc, \q trong vùng đất khô cằn không có nước.

decisions.choice: knew you: cared for you as my own
alternatives: knew about you
decisions.reason: To "know" a person can mean to choose them and look after them (Amos 3:2; Psalm 1:6). God's care for Israel in the wilderness is told in Deuteronomy 2:7 and 8:15.

decisions.choice: the Hebrew "I knew you"
alternatives: "I shepherded you" (the Septuagint and other ancient versions)
decisions.reason: The Greek and some other ancient versions read "I shepherded you", from a Hebrew verb that looks much like "I knew you". That reading fits the "pasture" of verse 6. The Hebrew text makes good sense as it stands and is followed here.

decisions.choice: a land of drought: burning, waterless country
decisions.reason: The word is found only here. It is related to words for heat and thirst, and Deuteronomy 8:15 describes the same wilderness as "thirsty ground where there was no water".

decisions.choice: cared for (B); took care of (R)
alternatives: knew
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "knew" means here (m1); Literal keeps "knew", which links to the knowing of God in verse 4.

source.text: כְּמַרְעִיתָם֙ וַיִּשְׂבָּ֔עוּ שָׂבְע֖וּ וַיָּ֣רָם לִבָּ֑ם עַל־כֵּ֖ן שְׁכֵחֽוּנִי׃

records.literal_gloss: According to their pasture, and they were satisfied; they were satisfied, and was lifted up their heart; therefore they forgot me.

en.L: As they had pasture, they were satisfied; \q they were satisfied, and their heart was lifted up; \q therefore they forgot {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: When they had pasture, they ate their fill; \q they were full, and their hearts grew proud; \q that is why they forgot {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: When I fed them, they had plenty to eat. \q But once they were full, they became proud, \q and they forgot {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

es.L: Conforme a sus pastos, se saciaron; \q se saciaron, y se enalteció su corazón; \q por eso se olvidaron de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.
es.B: Cuando tuvieron pastos, comieron hasta saciarse; \q se llenaron, y su corazón se volvió orgulloso; \q por eso se olvidaron de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.
es.R: Cuando los alimenté, tuvieron comida en abundancia. \q Pero una vez que se llenaron, se volvieron orgullosos, \q y se olvidaron de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}.

ko.L: 그들이 먹을 풀을 얻자 배가 불렀고, \q 배가 부르자 그들의 마음이 높아졌다. \q 그러므로 그들이 나를 잊었다.
ko.B: 그들은 꼴을 얻자 배불리 먹었고, \q 배가 부르자 마음이 교만해졌다. \q 그래서 그들은 나를 잊었다.
ko.R: 내가 그들을 먹이자 그들은 넉넉히 먹었다. \q 그러나 배가 부르자 교만해졌다. \q 그리고 나를 잊어버렸다.

fr.L: Selon leur pâturage, ils se sont rassasiés ; \q ils se sont rassasiés, et leur cœur s’est élevé ; \q c’est pourquoi ils {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}ont oublié.
fr.B: Quand ils avaient du pâturage, ils mangeaient à satiété ; \q une fois rassasiés, leur cœur s’est enorgueilli ; \q voilà pourquoi ils {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}ont oublié.
fr.R: Quand je les ai nourris, ils ont eu beaucoup à manger. \q Mais une fois rassasiés, ils sont devenus orgueilleux, \q et ils {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}ont oublié.

sw.L: Kwa kadiri ya malisho yao, walishiba; \q walishiba, na moyo wao ukainuka; \q kwa hiyo walinisahau.
sw.B: Walipokuwa na malisho, walikula wakashiba; \q walishiba, na mioyo yao ikajivuna; \q ndiyo sababu walinisahau.
sw.R: Nilipowalisha, walipata chakula tele. \q Lakini walipokwisha kushiba, wakawa na kiburi, \q nao wakanisahau.

vi.L: Khi có đồng cỏ, chúng no nê; \q chúng no nê, và lòng chúng tự cao; \q vì thế chúng đã quên {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.B: Khi có đồng cỏ, chúng ăn no nê; \q đã no rồi, lòng chúng sinh kiêu ngạo; \q vì thế chúng đã quên {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.R: Khi {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} nuôi chúng, chúng có dư dật để ăn. \q Nhưng khi đã no nê, chúng trở nên kiêu ngạo, \q và chúng quên {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.

decisions.choice: full, proud and forgetful: the danger Moses warned of
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 8:11-14 warns that when Israel has eaten and is satisfied, its heart will be lifted up and it will forget the LORD; 31:20 and 32:15 say the same. Hosea says that it has happened (compare 2:10, 15).

decisions.choice: their heart was lifted up: they became proud
decisions.reason: A heart that is "lifted up" is a proud heart (Deuteronomy 8:14; Ezekiel 28:2).

decisions.choice: When I fed them
alternatives: As they had pasture
decisions.reason: The pasture is the food God gave in the wilderness (verse 5). Readable says so, and drops the picture of sheep at pasture, which Literal and Balanced keep.

source.text: וָאֱהִ֥י לָהֶ֖ם כְּמוֹ־שָׁ֑חַל כְּנָמֵ֖ר עַל־דֶּ֥רֶךְ אָשֽׁוּר׃

records.literal_gloss: And I became to them like a lion; like a leopard on [the] road I will watch.

en.L: And I have become to them like a lion; \q like a leopard by the road I will watch [for them].
en.B: So I have become like a lion to them; \q like a leopard I will lurk beside the road.
en.R: So I have become like a lion to them. \q I will wait beside the road like a leopard, ready to attack.

es.L: Y he sido para ellos como un león; \q como un leopardo junto al camino [los] acecharé.
es.B: Por eso he sido para ellos como un león; \q como un leopardo acecharé junto al camino.
es.R: Por eso me he vuelto como un león para ellos. \q Esperaré junto al camino como un leopardo, listo para atacar.

ko.L: 그래서 나는 그들에게 사자처럼 되었다. \q 표범처럼 길가에서 [그들을] 노리겠다.
ko.B: 그래서 나는 그들에게 사자처럼 되었다. \q 표범처럼 길가에 숨어 노리겠다.
ko.R: 그래서 나는 그들에게 사자처럼 되었다. \q 나는 표범처럼 길가에서 기다리다가 덮치겠다.

fr.L: Et je suis devenu pour eux comme un lion ; \q comme un léopard sur le chemin je [les] guetterai.
fr.B: Alors je suis devenu pour eux comme un lion ; \q comme un léopard, je les guetterai au bord du chemin.
fr.R: Alors je suis devenu comme un lion pour eux. \q J’attendrai au bord du chemin comme un léopard, prêt à attaquer.

sw.L: Nami nimekuwa kwao kama simba; \q kama chui kando ya njia nitawavizia.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo nimekuwa kama simba kwao; \q kama chui nitawavizia kando ya njia.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo nimekuwa kama simba kwao. \q Nitangoja kando ya njia kama chui, tayari kuwashambulia.

vi.L: Vì vậy {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã trở nên như sư tử đối với chúng; \q như con báo bên đường, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ rình [chúng].
vi.B: Vì thế {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã trở nên như sư tử đối với chúng; \q như con báo, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ rình rập bên đường.
vi.R: Vì thế {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã trở nên như sư tử đối với chúng. \q Ta sẽ rình chờ bên đường như con báo, sẵn sàng vồ mồi.

decisions.choice: I have become: God has already turned against them, and the attack is still to come
alternatives: I will become (taking the verb as a future, as many do)
decisions.reason: The first verb is a past form and the second a future. Together they say that God now stands against Israel like a wild animal and will strike. The same pictures are used in 5:14.

decisions.choice: I will watch: lie in wait for prey
alternatives: "Assyria" (the same letters, read differently, as the Septuagint does)
decisions.reason: The verb means to watch closely, here as an animal watches for prey (Jeremiah 5:6). Its letters are the same as the name Assyria, and the Greek reads "the Assyrians". The sound may be meant to recall the empire through which God would strike. In 14:9 the same verb is used for God watching over Ephraim to care for him.

decisions.choice: lion, leopard and bear (verse 8): the most dangerous wild animals of the land
decisions.reason: All three lived in the hills and thickets of Israel in Hosea's time (1 Samuel 17:34; Jeremiah 5:6; Amos 5:19). Hosea has already pictured God as a lion against Ephraim in 5:14.

decisions.choice: ready to attack
decisions.reason: Readable says why the leopard waits beside the road (m2).

source.text: אֶפְגְּשֵׁם֙ כְּדֹ֣ב שַׁכּ֔וּל וְאֶקְרַ֖ע סְג֣וֹר לִבָּ֑ם וְאֹכְלֵ֥ם שָׁם֙ כְּלָבִ֔יא חַיַּ֥ת הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה תְּבַקְּעֵֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: I will meet them like a bear bereaved, and I will tear the enclosure of their heart, and I will devour them there like a lion; the animal of the field will rip them open.

en.L: I will meet them like a bear robbed of [her cubs], \q and I will tear open the enclosure of their heart; \q and I will devour them there like a lioness; \q the wild animal will rip them apart.
en.B: I will attack them like a bear robbed of her cubs \q and tear open their chests; \q I will devour them there like a lioness; \q wild animals will tear them to pieces.
en.R: I will attack them like a mother bear whose cubs have been taken. \q I will tear open their chests. \q I will eat them up like a lion. \q Wild animals will tear them to pieces.

es.L: Los encontraré como una osa privada de [sus crías], \q y les desgarraré el cerco de su corazón; \q y allí los devoraré como una leona; \q la fiera del campo los despedazará.
es.B: Los atacaré como una osa a la que le han robado las crías \q y les abriré el pecho; \q allí los devoraré como una leona; \q los animales salvajes los harán pedazos.
es.R: Los atacaré como una osa a la que le han quitado sus cachorros. \q Les abriré el pecho. \q Me los comeré como un león. \q Los animales salvajes los harán pedazos.

ko.L: 내가 새끼를 빼앗긴 곰처럼 그들을 만나서, \q 그들의 가슴을 찢어 열고, \q 거기에서 암사자처럼 그들을 삼키겠다. \q 들짐승이 그들을 찢을 것이다.
ko.B: 내가 새끼를 빼앗긴 곰처럼 그들에게 달려들어 \q 그들의 가슴을 찢어 놓고, \q 거기에서 암사자처럼 그들을 삼키겠다. \q 들짐승들이 그들을 갈기갈기 찢을 것이다.
ko.R: 나는 새끼를 빼앗긴 어미 곰처럼 그들에게 달려들겠다. \q 그들의 가슴을 찢어 놓겠다. \q 사자처럼 그들을 먹어 치우겠다. \q 들짐승들이 그들을 갈기갈기 찢을 것이다.

fr.L: Je les rencontrerai comme une ourse privée de [ses petits], \q et je déchirerai l’enveloppe de leur cœur ; \q et là je les dévorerai comme une lionne ; \q la bête des champs les mettra en pièces.
fr.B: Je les attaquerai comme une ourse privée de ses petits \q et je leur ouvrirai la poitrine ; \q là je les dévorerai comme une lionne ; \q les bêtes sauvages les mettront en pièces.
fr.R: Je les attaquerai comme une mère ourse à qui on a pris ses petits. \q Je leur ouvrirai la poitrine. \q Je les dévorerai comme un lion. \q Les bêtes sauvages les mettront en pièces.

sw.L: Nitakutana nao kama dubu aliyenyang'anywa [watoto wake], \q {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nitararua kifuniko cha moyo wao; \q {{deity_pronoun:nami|Nami}} nitawala huko kama simba jike; \q mnyama wa mwituni atawararua.
sw.B: Nitawashambulia kama dubu aliyenyang'anywa watoto wake \q na kuvirarua vifua vyao; \q nitawala huko kama simba jike; \q wanyama wa porini watawararua vipande vipande.
sw.R: Nitawashambulia kama dubu jike aliyenyang'anywa watoto wake. \q Nitavirarua vifua vyao. \q Nitawala kama simba. \q Wanyama wa porini watawararua vipande vipande.

vi.L: Ta sẽ gặp chúng như gấu cái bị cướp mất [con], \q và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ xé toang lồng bao quanh tim chúng; \q và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ ăn nuốt chúng tại đó như sư tử cái; \q thú hoang sẽ xé chúng ra.
vi.B: Ta sẽ tấn công chúng như gấu cái bị cướp mất con \q và xé toang lồng ngực chúng; \q {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ ăn nuốt chúng tại đó như sư tử cái; \q thú hoang sẽ xé chúng ra từng mảnh.
vi.R: Ta sẽ tấn công chúng như gấu mẹ bị bắt mất con. \q Ta sẽ xé toang lồng ngực chúng. \q Ta sẽ ăn nuốt chúng như sư tử. \q Thú hoang sẽ xé chúng ra từng mảnh.

decisions.choice: a bear robbed of her cubs: a picture of the fiercest anger
decisions.reason: A mother bear that has lost her young was proverbial for her fury (2 Samuel 17:8; Proverbs 17:12).

decisions.choice: the enclosure of their heart: the chest, the rib cage around the heart
alternatives: the covering of their heart, that is, their stubbornness
decisions.reason: The word means something that closes or encloses. With "heart" it most likely means the chest, which a wild animal tears open. Some take it as a picture of a closed, hard heart, but the context is the attack of animals.

decisions.choice: lioness; the wild animal: the animals as God's instruments of judgment
alternatives: lion
decisions.reason: The word for lion here is a less common one that may refer to a lioness. "The animal of the field" is a wild animal; in 2:14 God says the wild animals will devour the vines of unfaithful Israel.

decisions.choice: attack them
alternatives: meet them
decisions.reason: The verb means to meet, often in a hostile way, as here. Balanced and Readable say "attack"; Literal keeps "meet".

records.literal_gloss: It has destroyed you, O Israel, that against me, against your help.

en.L: It has destroyed you, O Israel, \q that [you are] against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, against your help.
en.B: You are destroyed, Israel, \q because you are against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, your helper.
en.R: Israel, you are ruined \q because you turned against {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, the one who helps you.

es.L: Te ha destruido, oh Israel, \q que [estés] contra {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, contra tu ayuda.
es.B: Estás destruido, Israel, \q porque estás contra {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, tu ayudador.
es.R: Israel, estás arruinado \q porque te pusiste en contra de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, el que te ayuda.

ko.L: 이스라엘아, 그것이 너를 망하게 했다. \q 네가 나를, 너를 돕는 이를 거스르기 [때문이다].
ko.B: 이스라엘아, 너는 망했다. \q 네가 너를 돕는 나를 거슬렀기 때문이다.
ko.R: 이스라엘아, 너는 망했다. \q 너를 돕는 나에게 네가 등을 돌렸기 때문이다.

fr.L: Cela t’a détruit, ô Israël, \q que [tu sois] contre {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, contre ton secours.
fr.B: Tu es détruit, Israël, \q parce que tu es contre {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, ton secours.
fr.R: Israël, tu es ruiné \q parce que tu t’es tourné contre {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, celui qui t’aide.

sw.L: Imekuangamiza, Ee Israeli, \q kwamba [u] dhidi {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, dhidi ya msaada wako.
sw.B: Umeangamizwa, Israeli, \q kwa sababu uko dhidi {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, msaidizi wako.
sw.R: Israeli, umeharibiwa \q kwa sababu ulinigeuka {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, ninayekusaidia.

vi.L: Điều ấy đã hủy diệt ngươi, hỡi Y-sơ-ra-ên, \q vì [ngươi] chống lại {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, chống lại Đấng giúp đỡ ngươi.
vi.B: Hỡi Y-sơ-ra-ên, ngươi bị hủy diệt \q vì ngươi chống lại {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, là Đấng giúp đỡ ngươi.
vi.R: Hỡi Y-sơ-ra-ên, ngươi đã bị hủy hoại \q vì ngươi đã chống lại {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, là Đấng giúp đỡ ngươi.

decisions.choice: Israel is destroyed because it has set itself against God, its helper
alternatives: "I will destroy you, Israel; who will help you?" (reading "who" for "that", as the Greek and Syriac versions seem to)
"Your destruction, Israel, is that you are against me"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is very short and hard to read: "it has destroyed you, Israel, that against me, against your help". The reading chosen keeps the Hebrew letters and takes the point to be that Israel's ruin comes from turning against the one who helps it. With a small change, the line becomes God's threat followed by a question. The verse is one of the hardest in the chapter.

decisions.choice: your help: God as the one who comes to Israel's aid
decisions.reason: The word is used of God's help to his people in Deuteronomy 33:26, 29 and Psalm 33:20. It sets God's help against the kings of verse 10, who cannot save.

source.text: אֱהִ֤י מַלְכְּךָ֙ אֵפ֔וֹא וְיוֹשִֽׁיעֲךָ֖ בְּכָל־עָרֶ֑יךָ וְשֹׁ֣פְטֶ֔יךָ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָמַ֔רְתָּ תְּנָה־לִּ֖י מֶ֥לֶךְ וְשָׂרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Where [is] your king then, and he will save you in all your cities, and your judges, of whom you said, give to me a king and princes?

en.L: Where [is] your king, then, \q that he may save you in all your cities? \q And [where are] your judges, about whom you said, \q "Give to me a king and princes"?
en.B: Where is your king now, \q who could save you in all your cities? \q Where are your rulers, of whom you said, \q "Give me a king and officials"?
en.R: Where is your king now? \q Let him save you in all your towns! \q Where are your leaders? \q You asked for them when you said, \q "Give us a king and officials!"

es.L: ¿Dónde [está] ahora tu rey, \q para que te salve en todas tus ciudades? \q ¿Y [dónde están] tus jueces, de los cuales dijiste: \q «Dame rey y príncipes»?
es.B: ¿Dónde está ahora tu rey, \q que te salve en todas tus ciudades? \q ¿Dónde están tus gobernantes, de quienes dijiste: \q «Dame un rey y jefes»?
es.R: ¿Dónde está ahora tu rey? \q ¡Que te salve en todas tus ciudades! \q ¿Dónde están tus dirigentes? \q Tú los pediste cuando dijiste: \q «¡Danos un rey y dirigentes!».

ko.L: 이제 네 왕이 어디 있느냐? \q 네 모든 성읍에서 너를 구원할 [자가]? \q 너희가 "나에게 왕과 고관들을 주십시오" 하고 말하던 \q 너의 재판관들은 [어디 있느냐]?
ko.B: 이제 네 왕이 어디 있느냐? \q 네 모든 성읍에서 너를 구원해 줄 왕이? \q 네가 "우리에게 왕과 관리들을 주십시오" 하고 말하던 \q 네 통치자들은 어디 있느냐?
ko.R: 이제 네 왕은 어디 있느냐? \q 그더러 네 모든 성읍에서 너를 구해 보라고 하여라! \q 네 지도자들은 어디 있느냐? \q 너희가 그들을 달라고 하지 않았느냐? \q "우리에게 왕과 관리들을 주십시오!" 하고 말이다.

fr.L: Où [est] donc ton roi, \q pour qu’il te sauve dans toutes tes villes ? \q Et [où sont] tes juges, dont tu as dit : \q « Donne-moi un roi et des chefs » ?
fr.B: Où est maintenant ton roi, \q qui pourrait te sauver dans toutes tes villes ? \q Où sont tes gouvernants, dont tu as dit : \q « Donne-moi un roi et des chefs » ?
fr.R: Où est ton roi maintenant ? \q Qu’il te sauve dans toutes tes villes ! \q Où sont tes dirigeants ? \q Tu les as demandés quand tu as dit : \q « Donne-nous un roi et des chefs ! »

sw.L: Yuko wapi basi mfalme wako, \q ili akuokoe katika miji yako yote? \q Na [wako wapi] waamuzi wako, ambao ulisema juu yao, \q "Nipe mfalme na wakuu"?
sw.B: Yuko wapi mfalme wako sasa, \q ambaye angeweza kukuokoa katika miji yako yote? \q Wako wapi watawala wako, ambao ulisema juu yao, \q "Nipe mfalme na wakuu"?
sw.R: Yuko wapi mfalme wako sasa? \q Na akuokoe katika miji yako yote! \q Wako wapi viongozi wako? \q Uliwaomba uliposema, \q "Tupe mfalme na viongozi!"

vi.L: Vậy vua của ngươi [ở] đâu, \q để người cứu ngươi trong mọi thành của ngươi? \q Và các thẩm phán của ngươi [ở đâu], những người mà ngươi đã nói: \q "Hãy ban cho tôi một vua và các quan trưởng"?
vi.B: Bây giờ vua của ngươi ở đâu, \q để cứu ngươi trong mọi thành của ngươi? \q Những người cai trị ngươi ở đâu, những người mà ngươi đã xin: \q "Hãy ban cho tôi một vua và các quan chức"?
vi.R: Bây giờ vua của ngươi đâu rồi? \q Hãy để vua ấy cứu ngươi trong mọi thành của ngươi! \q Những nhà lãnh đạo của ngươi đâu? \q Ngươi đã xin họ khi ngươi nói: \q "Hãy ban cho chúng tôi một vua và các quan chức!"

decisions.choice: where: a rare form of the word "where", used again in 13:14
alternatives: "I will be" (as some ancient versions read it)
decisions.reason: The form is unusual, but the question that follows ("where is your king?") shows that it means "where". The same form begins the questions to death and Sheol in 13:14.

decisions.choice: "Give me a king and princes": Israel's demand for a king in 1 Samuel 8
alternatives: the northern tribes' choice of their own kings after Solomon (1 Kings 12:20)
decisions.reason: The people asked Samuel for a king "to judge us like all the nations" (1 Samuel 8:5, 19-20). The northern kingdom later made its own kings without God (8:4). In Hosea's time its kings were murdered one after another (7:7; 2 Kings 15:8-30), and none of them could save it.

decisions.choice: your judges: rulers in general, not the judges of the time before the kings
decisions.reason: The word means those who govern and decide cases. It is used for Israel's leaders in 7:7 and Amos 2:3.

decisions.choice: Let him save you ...!; Give us
alternatives: that he may save you; Give me
decisions.reason: Readable turns the purpose clause into a mocking challenge, which is its point. It says "us" because the people speak as one ("me" in the Hebrew).

decisions.choice: "príncipes" (L); "jefes" (B); "dirigentes" (R)
decisions.reason: Sarim with the words of the Spanish prophets; the demand recalls 1 Samuel 8.

decisions.choice: The people's request is in 합쇼체 ("주십시오")
decisions.reason: The demand of 1 Samuel 8 was made to Samuel and so to God; people speak to a prophet and to God in 합쇼체.

records.literal_gloss: I give to you a king in my anger, and I take [him] away in my wrath.

en.L: I give you a king in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger, \q and I take [him] away in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} wrath.
en.B: I give you a king in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} anger, \q and in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} fury I take him away.
en.R: In anger I give you kings, \q and in fury I take them away.

es.L: Te doy rey en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} ira, \q y [te lo] quito en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} furor.
es.B: Te doy un rey en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} ira, \q y en {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} furor te lo quito.
es.R: Con enojo te doy reyes, \q y con furia te los quito.

ko.L: 내가 내 분노 가운데 너에게 왕을 주고, \q 내 진노 가운데 [그를] 빼앗는다.
ko.B: 나는 분노하여 너에게 왕을 주고, \q 진노하여 그를 빼앗는다.
ko.R: 나는 화가 나서 너희에게 왕들을 주고, \q 분노하여 그들을 빼앗는다.

fr.L: Je te donne un roi dans {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} colère, \q et je [l’]enlève dans {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} fureur.
fr.B: Je te donne un roi dans {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} colère, \q et dans {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} fureur je te l’enlève.
fr.R: Dans {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} colère, je te donne des rois, \q et dans {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} fureur, je te les enlève.

sw.L: Ninakupa mfalme katika hasira {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, \q na ninamwondoa katika ghadhabu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}.
sw.B: Ninakupa mfalme katika hasira {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, \q na katika ghadhabu {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} ninamwondoa.
sw.R: Kwa hasira ninakupa wafalme, \q na kwa ghadhabu ninawaondoa.

vi.L: Ta ban cho ngươi một vua trong cơn giận của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, \q và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cất [vua ấy] đi trong cơn thịnh nộ của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.B: Ta ban cho ngươi một vua trong cơn giận của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, \q và trong cơn thịnh nộ {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cất vua ấy đi.
vi.R: Trong cơn giận, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} ban cho ngươi các vua, \q và trong cơn thịnh nộ, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} cất họ đi.

decisions.choice: I give ... I take away: what God does again and again with Israel's kings
alternatives: the past: God gave Saul in anger and took him away
the coming end of the monarchy: the last king of Israel will be taken away
decisions.reason: The verbs are in a form that can describe repeated action. The northern kingdom had many kings who came and went by murder (2 Kings 15:8-30). The words may also look back to Saul, given when Israel rejected God as king (1 Samuel 8:7; 15:23), or forward to Hoshea, the last king, taken prisoner by Assyria (2 Kings 17:4).

decisions.choice: kings ... them
alternatives: a king ... him
decisions.reason: Readable uses the plural to make plain that this happens again and again (m1), and leaves out "my" with anger and fury, which is clear from "I".

records.literal_gloss: Bound up [is the] iniquity of Ephraim; stored up [is] his sin.

en.L: The iniquity of Ephraim is bound up; \q his sin is stored away.
en.B: Ephraim's guilt is wrapped up; \q his sin is kept in store.
en.R: The sins of Ephraim are tied up in a bundle. \q They are stored away and not forgotten.

es.L: Atada está la iniquidad de Efraín; \q guardado está su pecado.
es.B: La culpa de Efraín está bien atada; \q su pecado está guardado.
es.R: Los pecados de Efraín están atados en un bulto. \q Están guardados y no se olvidan.

ko.L: 에브라임의 죄악이 묶여 있고, \q 그의 죄가 쌓여 있다.
ko.B: 에브라임의 죄는 꽁꽁 싸매어 있고, \q 그의 죄는 고스란히 쌓여 있다.
ko.R: 에브라임의 죄는 한 묶음으로 묶여 있다. \q 그 죄는 잊히지 않고 쌓여 있다.

fr.L: L’iniquité d’Éphraïm est liée ; \q son péché est mis en réserve.
fr.B: La faute d’Éphraïm est enveloppée ; \q son péché est gardé en réserve.
fr.R: Les péchés d’Éphraïm sont attachés ensemble comme un paquet. \q Ils sont mis de côté et ne seront pas oubliés.

sw.L: Uovu wa Efraimu umefungwa; \q dhambi yake imewekwa akiba.
sw.B: Hatia ya Efraimu imefungwa; \q dhambi yake imehifadhiwa.
sw.R: Dhambi za Efraimu zimefungwa katika furushi. \q Zimewekwa akiba, wala hazijasahauliwa.

vi.L: Sự gian ác của Ép-ra-im đã được gói lại; \q tội lỗi nó được cất giữ.
vi.B: Tội lỗi của Ép-ra-im đã được gói kỹ; \q tội của nó được cất giữ để dành.
vi.R: Tội lỗi của Ép-ra-im được gói lại thành một bó. \q Chúng được cất giữ và không bị quên đi.

decisions.choice: bound up and stored away: kept safe for the day of judgment, not forgotten
decisions.reason: Valuables and documents were tied in a bag or rolled and sealed to be kept (Job 14:17; Deuteronomy 32:34). Ephraim's sin is not lost or overlooked; it is kept, ready to be dealt with.

decisions.choice: tied up in a bundle ... not forgotten
decisions.reason: Readable explains the picture of something tied up and stored (m1).

source.text: חֶבְלֵ֥י יֽוֹלֵדָ֖ה יָבֹ֣אוּ ל֑וֹ הוּא־בֵן֙ לֹ֣א חָכָ֔ם כִּֽי־עֵ֥ת לֹֽא־יַעֲמֹ֖ד בְּמִשְׁבַּ֥ר בָּנִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: Pains of one giving birth will come to him; he [is] a son not wise, for [the] time he does not stand at [the] breaking forth of children.

en.L: The pains of a woman giving birth come for him; \q he [is] a son who is not wise, \q for at the time he does not stand in the opening of the womb.
en.B: The pains of childbirth come upon him, \q but he is a child without sense; \q when the time comes, he does not move into the opening of the womb.
en.R: Pain comes on Ephraim like a woman in labor. \q But Ephraim is like a foolish baby \q that will not come out of the womb when it is time to be born.

es.L: Dolores de mujer que da a luz le vienen; \q él [es] un hijo no sabio, \q porque al tiempo no se presenta a la salida del vientre.
es.B: Le llegan los dolores del parto, \q pero es un hijo sin juicio; \q cuando llega el momento, no se coloca para salir del vientre.
es.R: El dolor le llega a Efraín como a una mujer de parto. \q Pero Efraín es como un bebé necio \q que no quiere salir del vientre cuando es hora de nacer.

ko.L: 해산하는 여자의 진통이 그에게 온다. \q 그는 지혜롭지 못한 아들이다. \q 때가 되었는데도 태의 문에 서지 않는다.
ko.B: 해산의 진통이 그에게 닥치지만, \q 그는 철없는 아이다. \q 때가 되어도 태에서 나오려 하지 않는다.
ko.R: 에브라임에게 해산하는 여자처럼 진통이 온다. \q 그러나 에브라임은 어리석은 아기와 같다. \q 태어날 때가 되었는데도 태에서 나오려 하지 않는다.

fr.L: Les douleurs d’une femme qui enfante viennent pour lui ; \q il [est] un fils qui n’est pas sage, \q car au moment [voulu] il ne se présente pas à l’ouverture du sein.
fr.B: Les douleurs de l’accouchement viennent sur lui, \q mais c’est un enfant sans intelligence ; \q quand le moment arrive, il ne se présente pas pour naître.
fr.R: La douleur vient sur Éphraïm comme sur une femme qui accouche. \q Mais Éphraïm est comme un bébé sans intelligence \q qui refuse de sortir du ventre de sa mère quand c’est le moment de naître.

sw.L: Utungu wa mwanamke anayezaa unamjia; \q yeye [ni] mwana asiye na hekima, \q kwa maana wakati ukifika hasimami katika mlango wa tumbo.
sw.B: Utungu wa kuzaa unamjia, \q lakini yeye ni mtoto asiye na akili; \q wakati unapofika, hasogei kwenye mlango wa tumbo.
sw.R: Maumivu yanamjia Efraimu kama mwanamke anayejifungua. \q Lakini Efraimu ni kama mtoto mjinga \q asiyetaka kutoka tumboni wakati wa kuzaliwa unapofika.

vi.L: Cơn đau của người đàn bà sinh nở đến trên nó; \q nó [là] đứa con không khôn ngoan, \q vì đến lúc, nó không đứng ở cửa lòng mẹ.
vi.B: Cơn đau sinh nở đến trên nó, \q nhưng nó là đứa con thiếu khôn ngoan; \q khi đến giờ, nó không chịu ra khỏi lòng mẹ.
vi.R: Cơn đau đến trên Ép-ra-im như người đàn bà chuyển dạ. \q Nhưng Ép-ra-im giống như đứa bé dại dột \q không chịu ra khỏi lòng mẹ khi đến lúc chào đời.

decisions.choice: a baby that will not be born: Ephraim has a moment when it could live, and it refuses
alternatives: the pains are only the pains of judgment, and the child picture is a separate saying
decisions.reason: The pains of labor are a common picture of sudden, unavoidable distress (Isaiah 13:8; Jeremiah 4:31). Here the picture turns: Ephraim is also the child, who does not come to the opening of the womb at the right time, which endangers its life. The same phrase for the opening of the womb is used in 2 Kings 19:3 and Isaiah 37:3. The crisis could lead to new life through turning back to God (14:2), but Ephraim does not take it.

decisions.choice: Ephraim is like ...
alternatives: him; he
decisions.reason: Readable names Ephraim and says "like" for both pictures, since the Hebrew moves from the mother's pain to the child without warning.

source.text: מִיַּ֤ד שְׁאוֹל֙ אֶפְדֵּ֔ם מִמָּ֖וֶת אֶגְאָלֵ֑ם אֱהִ֨י דְבָרֶיךָ֜מָ֗וֶת אֱהִ֤י קָֽטָבְךָ֙ שְׁא֔וֹל נֹ֖חַם יִסָּתֵ֥ר מֵעֵינָֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: From [the] hand of Sheol will I ransom them? From death will I redeem them? Where [are] your plagues, O death? Where [is] your destruction, O Sheol? Compassion is hidden from my eyes.

en.L: From the hand of Sheol shall I ransom them? \q From death shall I redeem them? \q Where [are] your plagues, O death? Where [is] your destruction, O Sheol? \q Compassion is hidden from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} eyes.
en.B: Shall I ransom them from the power of Sheol? \q Shall I redeem them from death? \q O death, where are your plagues? O Sheol, where is your sting? \q Compassion is hidden from {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} eyes.
en.R: Should I rescue them from the power of the grave? \q Should I set them free from death? \q Death, where are your plagues? Grave, where is your deadly sting? \q I will not change {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} mind and show pity.

es.L: ¿De la mano del Seol los rescataré? \q ¿De la muerte los redimiré? \q ¿Dónde [están] tus plagas, oh muerte? ¿Dónde [está] tu destrucción, oh Seol? \q La compasión está escondida de {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} ojos.
es.B: ¿Los rescataré del poder del lugar de los muertos? \q ¿Los redimiré de la muerte? \q Muerte, ¿dónde están tus plagas? Lugar de los muertos, ¿dónde está tu aguijón? \q La compasión está escondida de {{deity_pronoun:mis|Mis}} ojos.
es.R: ¿Debería rescatarlos del poder del sepulcro? \q ¿Debería librarlos de la muerte? \q Muerte, ¿dónde están tus plagas? Sepulcro, ¿dónde está tu aguijón mortal? \q No cambiaré de parecer ni tendré piedad.

ko.L: 내가 그들을 스올의 손에서 속량하겠느냐? \q 죽음에서 구속하겠느냐? \q 죽음아, 네 재앙들이 어디 있느냐? 스올아, 네 멸망이 어디 있느냐? \q 긍휼이 내 눈에서 숨겨졌다.
ko.B: 내가 그들을 스올의 권세에서 속량하겠느냐? \q 죽음에서 구속하겠느냐? \q 죽음아, 네 재앙들이 어디 있느냐? 스올아, 네 독침이 어디 있느냐? \q 내 눈에는 긍휼이 보이지 않는다.
ko.R: 내가 그들을 죽은 사람들이 있는 곳의 권세에서 구해 내야 하겠느냐? \q 죽음에서 건져 내야 하겠느냐? \q 죽음아, 네 재앙들이 어디 있느냐? 죽은 사람들이 있는 곳아, 너의 무서운 독침이 어디 있느냐? \q 나는 마음을 바꾸어 불쌍히 여기지 않겠다.

fr.L: De la main du Shéol les rachèterai-je ? \q De la mort les délivrerai-je ? \q Où [sont] tes fléaux, ô mort ? Où [est] ta destruction, ô Shéol ? \q La compassion est cachée à {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} yeux.
fr.B: Les rachèterai-je du pouvoir du séjour des morts ? \q Les délivrerai-je de la mort ? \q Mort, où sont tes fléaux ? Séjour des morts, où est ton aiguillon ? \q La compassion est cachée à {{deity_pronoun:mes|Mes}} yeux.
fr.R: Devrais-je les délivrer du pouvoir du séjour des morts ? \q Devrais-je les libérer de la mort ? \q Mort, où sont tes fléaux ? Séjour des morts, où est ton dard mortel ? \q Je ne changerai pas d’avis, je n’aurai pas pitié.

sw.L: Je, nitawafidia kutoka mkononi mwa Kuzimu? \q Je, nitawakomboa kutoka kifo? \q Ewe kifo, mapigo yako yako wapi? Ewe Kuzimu, maangamizi yako yako wapi? \q Huruma imefichwa machoni {{deity_pronoun:pangu|Pangu}}.
sw.B: Je, niwafidie kutoka nguvu za Kuzimu? \q Je, niwakomboe kutoka kifo? \q Ewe kifo, mapigo yako yako wapi? Ewe Kuzimu, mwiba wako uko wapi? \q Huruma imefichwa machoni {{deity_pronoun:pangu|Pangu}}.
sw.R: Je, niwaokoe kutoka nguvu za kaburi? \q Je, niwaweke huru kutoka kifo? \q Kifo, mapigo yako yako wapi? Kaburi, mwiba wako wa kuua uko wapi? \q Sitabadili nia {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} na kuwahurumia.

vi.L: Ta sẽ chuộc chúng khỏi tay Âm Phủ sao? \q Ta sẽ cứu chuộc chúng khỏi sự chết sao? \q Hỡi sự chết, các tai vạ của ngươi ở đâu? Hỡi Âm Phủ, sự hủy diệt của ngươi ở đâu? \q Lòng thương xót bị che khuất khỏi mắt {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.B: Ta có nên chuộc chúng khỏi quyền lực Âm Phủ không? \q Ta có nên cứu chuộc chúng khỏi sự chết không? \q Hỡi sự chết, đâu là các tai vạ của ngươi? Hỡi Âm Phủ, đâu là nọc độc của ngươi? \q Lòng thương xót đã khuất khỏi mắt {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}.
vi.R: Ta có nên giải cứu chúng khỏi quyền lực của nơi người chết không? \q Ta có nên giải thoát chúng khỏi sự chết không? \q Này sự chết, các tai vạ của ngươi đâu rồi? Này nơi của người chết, nọc độc chết người của ngươi đâu rồi? \q Ta sẽ không đổi ý mà thương xót nữa.

decisions.choice: questions: God asks whether he should rescue them from Sheol and death, and the answer is no
alternatives: promises: "I will ransom them from the power of Sheol; I will redeem them from death"
decisions.reason: Hebrew has no question word here; it can ask a question by tone alone, so the lines may be questions or promises. The verses around them are judgment (13:12-13, 15; 14:1), and the verse ends "compassion is hidden from my eyes", which fits a refusal. Read as promises, the lines would be a sudden burst of hope, like 11:8-9, in the middle of the judgment, and the rest of the verse would mock death. Both readings are possible, and the text does not settle it.

decisions.choice: Where are your plagues, O death?: God calls on death and Sheol to bring their plagues against Israel
alternatives: a taunt over death, which has lost its power (the sense in 1 Corinthians 15:55)
"I will be your plagues, O death; I will be your destruction, O Sheol" (reading the first word as "I will be")
decisions.reason: "Where" is the same rare form as in 13:10 ("Where is your king?"). If the first lines refuse rescue (m1), these lines summon death to do its work: "Come, death, where are your plagues?" If the first lines promise rescue, these lines taunt death. Some ancient translations, the Latin among them, read the word as "I will be", which makes God himself the end of death. The reading chosen follows m1.

decisions.choice: plagues ... destruction: deadly disease and ruin, the weapons of death
decisions.reason: The first word is the usual word for a deadly plague or epidemic. The second is a rarer word for a destroying blow or pestilence; it is paired with plague in Psalm 91:6 and used of "bitter destruction" in Deuteronomy 32:24.

decisions.choice: compassion is hidden from my eyes: God will not relent
alternatives: their repentance is hidden from my eyes
decisions.reason: The word for compassion is found only here. It comes from the verb used when God relents or is moved to pity, as in 11:8 ("my compassion is stirred"). To have it "hidden from my eyes" means God will not change his mind about the judgment.

decisions.choice: quoted in 1 Corinthians 15:55, where Paul follows the Greek and uses the words as a taunt over death
decisions.reason: Paul writes "Where, O death, is your victory? Where, O death, is your sting?" He follows the Greek of Hosea, which has "sting" in the second question (and "penalty" in the first), puts "victory" from Isaiah 25:8 in place of "plagues", and speaks to death both times where Hosea has Sheol. In Paul's chapter Christ's resurrection has defeated death. The translation here follows the Hebrew; whatever Hosea meant in his own setting (m1, m2), Paul's use shows how the verse was read in the light of the resurrection.

decisions.choice: sting (B); deadly sting (R)
alternatives: destruction
pestilence
decisions.reason: The word is a deadly blow (m3). Balanced and Readable say "sting", which gives a sharp, fatal attack in one word and keeps the line recognizable beside 1 Corinthians 15:55 (m5); it does not take over Paul's meaning. Literal keeps "destruction". A reviewer should decide whether "sting" goes too far from the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: the grave; I will not change my mind and show pity
alternatives: Sheol; compassion is hidden from my eyes
decisions.reason: Readable says "the grave" for Sheol, the place of the dead, as in Isaiah. It says plainly what "compassion is hidden from my eyes" means (m4).

decisions.choice: "¿Dónde [están] tus plagas, oh muerte? ¿Dónde [está] tu destrucción, oh Seol?" (L); "aguijón" (B), "aguijón mortal" (R)
decisions.reason: As the terms note sets: Literal follows the Hebrew; Balanced and Readable use "aguijón", the word of the Spanish 1 Corinthians 15:55, which quotes this verse from the Greek. Sheol is "Seol" at Literal and "el lugar de los muertos" at Balanced, as the Spanish prophets have it; Readable says "sepulcro" here, as the terms note sets.

decisions.choice: "Où ..., ô mort ?" (L), "Mort, où ... ?" (B, R), with "aiguillon" (B) and "dard" (R) as the published 1 Corinthians 15:55; Sheol "le Shéol" (L), "le séjour des morts" (B, R)
alternatives: "ô tombeau"
decisions.reason: Paul quotes these questions from the Greek as a taunt over death; here they summon death against Israel, but the French shares the New Testament's form and words so the quotation can be seen.

decisions.choice: "Ewe kifo ... Ewe Kuzimu" (L, B); "Kifo ... Kaburi" (R); "mwiba wako" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's wording: "kifo" and "mwiba" (sting) as 1 Corinthians 15:55, which quotes these lines from the Greek as a taunt over death (m5). Sheol is "Kuzimu", and Readable says "kaburi" (the grave), as the English Readable. In Hosea the questions call death to bring its plagues (m2).

decisions.choice: "Hỡi sự chết, ... ở đâu?" (L); "Hỡi sự chết, đâu là ...?" (B); "Này sự chết, ... đâu rồi?" (R); Sheol "Âm Phủ" (L, B), "nơi của người chết" (R)
decisions.reason: The shape of each level follows the published 1 Corinthians 15:55, which quotes this line from the Greek ("chiến thắng", "nọc độc"); the Hebrew has "plagues" and "destruction", and Balanced and Readable take "nọc độc" for the second, as the English takes "sting". Sheol follows the Isaiah note.

decisions.choice: "죽음아, 네 … 어디 있느냐?" as the Korean 1 Corinthians 15:55, with "독침" for the sting (B, R) as there; Sheol "스올" (L, B), "죽은 사람들이 있는 곳" (R)
alternatives: "사망아"
decisions.reason: The Korean 1 Corinthians 15:55 reads "죽음아, 네 승리가 어디 있느냐?" and "죽음아, 네 독침이 어디 있느냐?", taking up these words from the Greek as a taunt over death. Here they summon death against Israel, so Korean keeps the shared address, question and "독침", but translates the Hebrew: "재앙들" for the plagues, Sheol rather than death in the second question, and "멸망" for the destruction at Literal. Sheol is worded as settled for the prophets.

decisions.choice: "속량하다" for *padah*, "구속하다" for *ga'al* (L, B)
decisions.reason: Two verbs for buying back, kept apart as in Isaiah; R says "구해 내다" and "건져 내다".

records.literal_gloss: For he among brothers flourishes; will come an east wind, wind of Yahweh, from [the] wilderness coming up, and will be ashamed his spring, and will be dried up his fountain; he will plunder [the] treasury of every vessel of desire.

en.L: Though he flourishes among brothers, \q an east wind will come, the wind of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, rising from the wilderness, \q and his spring will fail, and his fountain will be dried up; \q he will plunder the treasury of every precious thing.
en.B: Though he thrives among his brothers, \q an east wind will come, a wind of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} blowing up from the desert; \q his spring will fail and his fountain dry up. \q An enemy will plunder his storehouse of every treasure.
en.R: Ephraim may do well among the other tribes, \q but {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} will send a hot wind from the east, blowing in from the desert. \q It will dry up Ephraim's springs and wells. \q An enemy will carry off all his treasures.

es.L: Aunque él florezca entre hermanos, \q vendrá el viento del este, el viento {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}}, que sube del desierto, \q y se secará su manantial, y se agotará su fuente; \q él saqueará el tesoro de todo objeto precioso.
es.B: Aunque prospere entre sus hermanos, \q vendrá un viento del este, un viento {{divine_name:del SEÑOR|de Yahvé}} que sopla desde el desierto; \q su manantial fallará y su fuente se secará. \q Un enemigo saqueará su depósito de todo tesoro.
es.R: Puede que a Efraín le vaya bien entre las otras tribus, \q pero {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} enviará un viento caliente del este que sopla desde el desierto. \q Secará los manantiales y los pozos de Efraín. \q Un enemigo se llevará todos sus tesoros.

ko.L: 그가 형제들 가운데서 번성하여도, \q 동풍이, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 바람이 광야에서 일어나 올 것이니, \q 그의 샘이 마르고 그의 우물이 말라 버릴 것이다. \q 그가 모든 귀한 그릇이 든 보물 창고를 약탈할 것이다.
ko.B: 그가 형제들 가운데서 번성하여도, \q 동풍이, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}의 바람이 사막에서 불어와 \q 그의 샘이 마르고 우물이 바닥날 것이다. \q 원수가 그의 창고에서 온갖 보물을 약탈해 갈 것이다.
ko.R: 에브라임이 다른 지파들 가운데서 잘된다 해도, \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}가 보내는 뜨거운 동풍이 사막에서 불어올 것이다. \q 그 바람이 에브라임의 샘과 우물을 말려 버릴 것이다. \q 원수가 그의 보물을 다 빼앗아 갈 것이다.

fr.L: Bien qu’il prospère parmi des frères, \q un vent d’est viendra, le vent {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}}, montant du désert, \q et sa source tarira, et sa fontaine sera desséchée ; \q il pillera le trésor de tout objet précieux.
fr.B: Même s’il prospère parmi ses frères, \q un vent d’est viendra, un vent {{divine_name:du SEIGNEUR|de Yahvé}} soufflant du désert ; \q sa source tarira et sa fontaine se desséchera. \q Un ennemi pillera son trésor, tous ses objets précieux.
fr.R: Éphraïm a beau réussir parmi les autres tribus, \q {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} enverra un vent brûlant de l’est, qui soufflera du désert. \q Il desséchera les sources et les puits d’Éphraïm. \q Un ennemi emportera tous ses trésors.

sw.L: Ingawa anastawi kati ya ndugu, \q upepo wa mashariki utakuja, upepo wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, ukipanda kutoka nyikani, \q na chemchemi yake itashindwa, na kisima chake kitakauka; \q yeye atateka hazina ya kila kitu cha thamani.
sw.B: Ingawa anastawi kati ya ndugu zake, \q upepo wa mashariki utakuja, upepo wa {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ukivuma kutoka jangwani; \q chemchemi yake itakoma na kisima chake kitakauka. \q Adui atateka ghala lake la kila hazina.
sw.R: Efraimu anaweza kufanikiwa kati ya makabila mengine, \q lakini {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} atatuma upepo wa joto kutoka mashariki, ukivuma kutoka jangwani. \q Utakausha chemchemi na visima vya Efraimu. \q Adui atachukua hazina zake zote.

vi.L: Dù nó thịnh vượng giữa anh em mình, \q gió đông sẽ đến, là gió của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}, thổi lên từ hoang mạc, \q và suối nó sẽ cạn, mạch nước nó sẽ khô; \q nó sẽ cướp kho tàng của mọi vật quý.
vi.B: Dù nó sinh sôi giữa anh em mình, \q gió đông sẽ đến, ngọn gió của {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} thổi lên từ sa mạc; \q suối nó sẽ cạn và mạch nước nó sẽ khô. \q Kẻ thù sẽ cướp sạch kho tàng của nó, mọi báu vật.
vi.R: Ép-ra-im có thể thịnh vượng giữa các chi tộc khác, \q nhưng {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} sẽ sai một ngọn gió nóng từ phương đông, thổi đến từ sa mạc. \q Gió ấy sẽ làm khô cạn các suối và giếng của Ép-ra-im. \q Kẻ thù sẽ cướp đi mọi báu vật của nó.

decisions.choice: he flourishes: a play on the name Ephraim, "fruitful"
decisions.reason: The verb sounds like the name Ephraim, which Genesis 41:52 explains as "God has made me fruitful". Hosea plays on the name again in 9:16 and 14:9. The flourishing plant will wither in the hot wind.

decisions.choice: among brothers: Ephraim's place among the tribes
alternatives: "among the reeds" (a very similar word, which would continue the plant picture)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "brothers". A word with almost the same letters means reed grass by the water (Genesis 41:2, 18), and many readers think it fits the picture of a plant that withers when its spring dries up. The Hebrew text is followed, and the alternative is noted.

decisions.choice: an east wind: the hot, dry desert wind, here a picture of Assyria
decisions.reason: The east wind blows in from the desert, withers plants and dries up water (Genesis 41:6; Ezekiel 17:10; 19:12). In 12:2 Ephraim "chases the east wind" in its dealings with Assyria. Calling it "the wind of the LORD" says that the invasion comes as God's judgment. Assyria took Samaria in 722 BC (2 Kings 17:5-6).

decisions.choice: his spring will fail: the verb usually means "be ashamed", used of water that disappoints
alternatives: "will dry up" (a verb that sounds the same)
decisions.reason: The verb is the usual one for being put to shame. It is used for those disappointed by dry cisterns (Jeremiah 14:3) and here of the spring itself. It also sounds like the verb "dry up", which follows in the next clause.

decisions.choice: he will plunder: the enemy that the east wind stands for
alternatives: the wind itself, as God's instrument
God himself
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "he". Plundering treasuries is what invading armies did (2 Kings 15:19-20; 17:3), so the subject is most likely the enemy the wind stands for (m3).

decisions.choice: An enemy will plunder (B); An enemy will carry off (R)
alternatives: He will plunder
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the plunderer as an enemy (m5), without naming Assyria. Readable also says "the other tribes" for "brothers", and says that the LORD sends the wind, which is what "the wind of the LORD" means.
